Description: Major sap-sucking pest of paddy causing hopper burn patches in dense, lush canopies.
Symptoms: Circular yellow patches rapidly turning brown ('hopper burn'); sooty mold at tiller bases; premature lodging in mature crop.

Description: Devastating fungal disease affecting leaves, nodes, and panicles during periods of high humidity and low night temperatures.
Symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with gray centers and reddish-brown margins; neck blast leading to blank chaffy panicles.

Description: Widespread micro-nutrient deficiency in submerged calcareous soils of Indo-Gangetic and Deccan plains.
Symptoms: Rust-colored reddish-brown pigmentation on 3rd and 4th leaves; stunted tillering; uneven plant height and delayed heading.

Description: Invasive voracious foliar caterpillar feeding aggressively inside the central whorls of maize plants.
Symptoms: Pin-hole punctures on young leaves, ragged shot-hole appearance, abundant sawdust-like fecal frass in whorls.

Description: Severe foliar disease causing large elliptical grayish-green or tan lesions across the maize canopy.
Symptoms: Long elliptical necrotic lesions (2-15 cm) on lower leaves progressing upwards; premature plant senescence.

Description: High-impact cool season fungal rust prevalent in Northern and Central wheat zones with cool humid weather.
Symptoms: Bright yellow pustules arranged in characteristic linear stripes on leaf blades; dusty yellow urediniospores rub off on touch.

Description: Colonies of green aphids congregating on developing ears and flag leaves during heading and grain filling.
Symptoms: Sticky honeydew and sooty mold on earheads; yellowing and curling of flag leaf; shriveled light-weight grain formation.

Description: Primary economic pest attacking flowers and developing pods of pigeonpea and chickpea.
Symptoms: Circular clean-cut holes bored into pods; caterpillars feeding with head inserted inside pod while body remains outside.

Description: Soil-borne vascular wilt causing sudden collapse of pigeonpea plants during flowering and podding.
Symptoms: Loss of turgidity in leaves, gradual yellowing and wilting, purple vertical band on stem base, dark brown vascular xylem discoloration.

Description: Nutrient disorder frequently observed in black cotton calcareous soils with high calcium carbonate and high pH.
Symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on youngest leaves turning bleached ivory-white; suppressed nodulation and poor pod formation.

Description: Whitefly-transmitted virus causing severe yield penalty in greengram and blackgram crops.
Symptoms: Irregular bright yellow and dark green mottled patches on young trifoliate leaves; puckered malformed leaves and few stunted pods.

Description: Early seedling pest attacking sorghum within 1 to 4 weeks after germination.
Symptoms: Drying and rotting of central growing shoot producing typical 'dead heart' that easily pulls out with foul odor; excessive tillering.
